items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But the embouchure that really puzzled me was Coltrane, and Johnny Hodges. It was a long time before I realized that they were playing double lip.

ctx.x: So, who knows? It may be. There seemed to be a similarity. They had that really tight thing, smile, and not everybody – a whole lot of cats don’t have that kind of embouchure.

No. Well, they can’t get the dexterity that they want with it, because you know, it’s an old saying, that in order to get the dexterity, you got to have your mouth so that the reed can vibrate freely. So that – that’s a myth. But the embouchure that really puzzled me was Coltrane, and Johnny Hodges. It was a long time before I realized that they were playing double lip.
